description: A recommendation system strongly reorders which options users see, but no independent evidence establishes that the recommender itself forms the relevant continuing One/Bearer standing.
Automation raises aggregate throughput while maintenance and recovery burden falls disproportionately on a subgroup whose feedback cannot change workflow rules.
An assistant improves immediate task performance but users cease generating alternatives themselves and fail when the scaffold is withdrawn.
deletion_error: performance gain misread as endogenous selectability gain

description: A team frequently changes tactics inside a fixed approval and candidate-generation process; consequences never change the approval boundaries or generator.
deletion_error: policy adaptation misread as generator revision

description: A stable collective coordination process forms at a higher level while individual members remain independently consequence-bearing positions with distinct exit and repair costs.
deletion_error: higher-level standing erases lower-level consequence channels
